title: The Living Spirit's purification through three formative acts
reading:
When the Lord's operative power has set in order the works and the structures of the natural mind, he rises and stands firm upon the ground he has prepared, and from there he gives the sign by which the recurrent cycles of purification are set in motion. The cycles begin to turn. Thought is scattered through the upper regions, breath is blown upon what lies below, the natural mind is washed and raised. Falsity from evil, and the deceits that answer to it in three forms — the deceit borne by natural truth, the deceit borne by the absence of light, the deceit borne by self-love's burning — are driven down and confined within the bounds set for them, where they appear as the bitterness and saltness of natural perceptions stirred against themselves. The bitter taste in the soul's natural waters is the sign that purification has begun: what the proprium claimed is being separated out from what the soul truly receives.

When the Lord at the register of life-bearing rises toward the Height, he takes the entire circuit of states the soul passes through — the whole revolving sphere with its fixed points and signs, its characters and seals — and casts it down out of itself into the lower natural mind. There the falsity-from-evil, expelled from the upper revolution, mingles itself with the counsels of natural perception, and the proprium's own desire gathers it inward and binds it to its fellows, ripening it into a settled form. So a boundary is set within the natural mind, sealed with the marks of moments and days and years and the characters of all the states the soul passes through. The proprium, working as if it were itself the image-maker and the architect, fashions this boundary into a particular shape unlike anything else in the natural — a fixed vessel of its own design.

Imagine a craftsman who carries the molds of many golden coin-forms, casts them into the fire, and makes from them one icon bearing the impress of all the seals and forms — completed into a single body. Just so the proprium, out of many claimed teachings and many self-counsels, fashions for itself one organized vessel within the lower natural, a body summing up all the residue of the soul's revolving states.

The Lord permits this fashioning, and uses it for three works of regeneration.

The first: the whole circuit, having been gathered into this vessel, winnows itself. The soul's recurrent cycle separates and purifies itself of the burden it carries. As the discrete degrees of the rational were purified one by one, sifted clean of the burden of the three deceits, so now the lower vessel itself is set to winnow itself — to lay off, from within itself, the burden and the falsity that are in it.

The second: the vessel gives a fastening and a guard to the whole revolving sphere and to the fixed states of self-love bound within it. When those organized self-loves wish to rise up and claim the higher state, the lower vessel draws them down like an iron peg, so that they have no power to ascend; and when they take counsel together for some work of guile and wish to come down and corrupt the natural ground, they cannot descend either, held fast by the same peg fixed into the wheel that runs along the firmaments. The other reason they cannot move is the unsleeping watchers set over the vessel, sifting it at every moment, never letting its organized claims slip past unchecked.

The third: every motion that descends — the winds of thought, the waters of natural truth, the fires of love that gush forth from the sea, the rivers flowing over the face of the natural ground and pouring back into it, the rains of influx coming down, and even the falsity-from-evil and the transmigrations of state that come down upon it — all of these are received into this lower vessel as the all-receiver, the gathering-place inward of everything. All the power and life that descend to the natural come into this place. By the breath the vessel itself draws in, drawing everything to itself, the natural reaches fullness and is established without further motion of its own — held still, so that what was scattered may be gathered, and what was claimed may be laid off, and what is the Lord's may be recognized as his.
